body:
A channel mints a manifest row naming a peer's schema export by hyperschema ENTITY, and two
stores that both publish a hyperschema of the same name file at the same default entity
(hyperschema:Plant). `classify` then resolves that row against whichever definition and
binding win at that entity across authors in the pool — so a peer's lens can resolve to the
RECEIVER's law before any address matching runs, and which side wins is decided by the peer's
own timestamps. T209's renderer path matches on the law's content address specifically to
avoid this, and that match cannot help when the address it is handed is already the
receiver's. The blessing door's entityCaptureRefusal guards a publish, not a federation edge.

Found by T209's build lane (2026-08-21), which named the gap in its rail file at the case
"a peer's app binds to the PEER's lens".

Build direction: entity namespacing at the edge — a channel's pool should file a peer's
definitions at entities that cannot collide with the receiver's. This changes what a channel
WRITES, so it interacts with T214's pool-seeding design ground; read that ticket first and
decide together if the sessions align.

Acceptance criteria:
(a) A peer and receiver both publishing hyperschema "Plant" federate without the peer's lens
    ever resolving to the receiver's law — the peer's rows file at a non-colliding entity, and
    the peer's lens answers the peer's data. Verify: new test in
    test/federation/entity-collision.test.ts (install-by-federation.test.ts is frozen).
(b) A receiver's own lens at the shared name is byte-untouched by the channel's filing
    (two-sided). Verify: same file.
(c) Existing pools with collided entities are carried by a migration or an honest refusal —
    decided at build time with the T214 alignment. Verify: named then.

Merge tier: changes what a channel writes — Myk's merge, with T214.
title: Peer and receiver file law at the same hyperschema entity — the receiver's law answers for the peer's
